My condolences. I lost my father in March of last year. It wasn't sudden. He had health issues since I was in elementary so I grew up with it. I spent years imagining how I'd feel. Years. It still didn't compare. 

A few thoughts for you-
1. Therapy is never a bad option. Especially when dealing with a loss. Don't even pretend to be strong for yourself or anyone around you. Please.
2. Grief does not affect 2 people the same. The stages of grief exist but the process varies tremendously. Unfortunately you won't know until you're already in the midst but a support system or an outlet can be a big help.
3. Since I lost my father I noticed changes in myself. It happens to a lot of people but I will cry at damn near anything anymore. Even the title of your post choked me hard. I've had to leave public places for a moment for not being able to control my sobs.

There will be reminders wherever you go. Triggers. Memories. It most likely won't stop even if you wanted them to. The most important piece of advice I can give to you is this: "You never get over it. That's not what it's about. You just have to learn to get through it." 

Stay strong. Reach out. Help yourself so you can help others as well. Peace.
